chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Rahman al-Khasha'i, who said:

I used to go to Ibn Abi Layla regarding our inheritance so that he would distribute it, and there was in it a withheld asset (habis), and he would delay/deny me. So when it prolonged, I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the return of the withheld asset and the enforcement of the inheritance?'

He (the narrator) said: So I went to him, and he did as he had done. So I said to him, 'I complained to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), and he said to me such and such.' He said: 'So Ibn Abi Layla made me swear an oath that he (peace be upon him) had indeed said that to you.' So I swore an oath to him, and he judged for me with that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on withheld assets (habis) in inheritance according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential authority of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in resolving practical legal disputes, specifically regarding the enforcement of inheritance rights against judicial delays. By citing the Prophet’s command to return withheld assets (habis), the Imam underscores the binding nature of prophetic precedent in Shia legal theory, demonstrating how Imams serve as the living interpreters of divine law in everyday transactions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdul Rahman Al Khash’amy who said,

‘I differed with Ibn Abu Layli with regards to inheritance for us in order to distribute it, and there was in it a withheld asset, and it had been handed over to me. So when the matter prolonged, I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or does he not know that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered with the return of a withheld asset and enforcement of the inheritance?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to him, and he did just as he had done. So I said to him, ‘I complained to Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me such and such’. He said, ‘So Ibn Abu Layli made me swear an oath that he<sup>asws</sup> had indeed said that’. So I swore an oath to him, so he judged for me with that’.
en.sarwar: 28. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Khath‘amiy who has narrated the following: “

About an issue of a legacy for distribution I once faced differences with ibn abu Layla’. In that legacy, there was an item on hold and he opposed me. When it prolonged I complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he said, ‘Did he not know that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, commanded to return items on hold and execute the rules of inheritance?’

I went to him and he did as before. I said, ‘I have complained before Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and he said so and so on the issue.’ Ibn abu Layla asked me to take oath that he (the Imam) has said so. I took the oath; then he judged accordingly.’”
